param_input_item.param_description: a matrix: square symmetric positive definite or Hermitian positive definite, dense or sparse.
a character vector or string: 'upper' (default) or 'lower', in any case and possibly shortened.

description.p: F = chol(A) factorizes symmetric positive definite matrixA into an upper triangular F that satisfies A = F' * F.
Sparse double, single, complex double, and complex single matrices are supported. Sparse factors keep sparse storage and keep the input numeric class where applicable.

[F, p] = chol(A) does not raise an error when the factorization fails: p is the index of the first failing pivot (0 on success) and F holds the factor of the first p - 1 rows and columns. For a sparse A, F keeps all its columns: it has p - 1 rows (columns with 'lower'), except a real tridiagonal matrix with all its sub and super diagonal entries, whose factor stays square with zero rows from p on.
A diagonal entry of a complex A with a nonzero imaginary part fails like a non positive pivot.
F = chol(A, 'lower') uses the lower triangle of A and returns a lower triangular F that satisfies A = F * F'.

history_item.history_description: added sparse single and complex single factorization support
